title: In-Context Scheming Invisible to Layer-Probes: Deception Shifts Representational Locus Between Layers

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Directly addresses whether deception probes are robust to representational locus shifts. If fine-tuning moves where deception is encoded, fixed-layer probes are unreliable, which has immediate implications for probe deployment strategy.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Training probes at every layer of GPT-2 medium is feasible with medium compute. Constructing deception datasets and fine-tuning are standard tasks. The main complexity is in the fine-tuning step to produce deceptive outputs, which requires careful dataset construction.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Clear deliverable: layer-by-layer probe accuracy plots before and after fine-tuning. However, the fine-tuning step adds scope and may not converge cleanly on a small model. Could be tightened by using pre-existing deception-fine-tuned checkpoints if available.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Novelty not assessed due to partial Wave 3 completion.
